label: read2-track-3
in_my_words: The project makes a prediction in advance about dog kidney cell balls. It says a simple model that only knows how many cells a ball has can predict how dented the hollow inside is, better than dumb guesses. It uses another team's public data and does no new lab work.
how_in_my_words: They download the 2021 paper's data and record file fingerprints. They fit a trend line on normal cells and lock the model's settings in a dated file. Then they compare the model with plain guesses (always round, the average, ball size alone) on cells it hasn't seen, holding out one photo day at a time. They will report the result whether it wins or loses. They haven't scored the model yet, so this is a plan, not a result.

test_questions.question: Has the locked model been scored on unseen cells?
test_questions.my_answer: No. Only the size-only line has been checked so far.

test_questions.question: Which plain guess is the hardest to beat?
Why can't they tell cell-type differences from day differences?
test_questions.my_answer: Each cell type was photographed on different days.

test_questions.question: What typical error did the size-only line get versus the plain average?
test_questions.my_answer: 0.1214 versus 0.1396, so the line is slightly better.

test_questions.question: What does the model's formula for wall length per cell look like?
test_questions.my_answer: Cannot say. The text gives no formula.

words_i_did_not_know: Lean / Lean proofs (half: a proof checker, but not why it matters here)
sentences_i_could_not_follow: Each cell brings a fixed length of inner wall. So the number of cells shapes the dents.

The 2021 authors ran their model many times with different settings, 243 in our check. We call this the published sweep. Even the best run fit normal cells worse than the plain average does. So our first check, which asks us to reproduce their model, may fail.
One formula in our plan was written upside down. We found the correct version and it matches to 14 decimal places. We must fix the plan before we start.
We keep a list of rules that a computer has checked, using a tool called Lean. That list has no rule about lumen shape. So no proof tool backs the biology here.
We left out one photo day at a time and tested on it.
what_would_help: Say the core idea in one concrete sentence first, for example why more cells would make the hollow rounder or more dented. Define "dentedness" and the 0 to 1 scale at first use. Say which formula was upside down and why it matters. Cut the Lean, law-library, ANOVA and ICC material or explain why a reader should care. Give one number a reader can picture for what "winning" means. The p-value and the error figures need a plain gloss.
